chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Nassaabi (one who hates the Ahl al-Bayt) was mentioned, so he said: Do not marry them, and do not eat their slaughtered meat, and do not reside with them.

key_terms.النّصَابُ: Nassaabi: One who is hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically denying or disparaging their rights.
key_terms.تَسْكُنُوا مَعَهُمْ: Do not reside with them: Prohibition of living in close proximity or cohabitation with the Nassaabi.
key_terms.تُنَاكِحُوهُمْ: Do not marry them: Prohibition of matrimonial alliance with the Nassaabi.
key_terms.ذَبَائِحَهُمْ: Their slaughtered meat: Prohibition of consuming meat slaughtered by the Nassaabi.

ai.seo_question: What are the three prohibitions regarding the Nassaabi according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In the context of the era of occultation and political strife, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineated the boundaries of *al-wala' wa al-baraa'* (alliance and disavowal) by prohibiting marriage, consumption of slaughtered meat, and cohabitation with the *Nassaabi*. This ruling underscores the jurisprudential principle that deep-seated enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt renders an individual distinct from the community of believers, affecting both personal status and social integration.
